=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:564-575 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The new `released_cycle_holds_pin` branch in pin_preflight() forces an unpinned run whenever a tracking issue is released, even when the `promote-cycle-frozen` tag still exists, and it runs before the wrapper and support pin checks (line 582); the smoke gate then dispatches on `main` with `cycle_baseline_sha="${main_tip}"` (lines 1072-1076, 1101-1128).
  WHY: The `internal-*.yml` wrappers still call `@promote-candidate`, and the follower keeps that branch frozen while the tag exists (default freeze cap 48h against a 24h hold cap; a lightweight or unparsable tag is never deleted), so the proving and verifying runs execute the old frozen code and the cycle can promote a `main` SHA they never exercised; all four reviewers rated it MAJOR (mapped to high).
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:754-775,910-936 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: promote_cycle_hold_guard() calls promote_cycle_hold_alert() synchronously in the per-issue release loop (call site line 936), and each call can block for up to 30s.
  WHY: The listing allows up to 100 issues; with 21 or more released issues each hitting the timeout, the wait passes 10.5 minutes, which is more than the 10-minute margin left under the 340-minute job cap (.github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml:124-126) after the default 30m idle wait and 5h gate wait; gemini, minimax and openai rated it MAJOR (mapped to high), while anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 judged it speculative and listed it only as a hardening suggestion.
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:810 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The err_line sanitisation `sed 's/::/: :/g'` replaces matches without overlap, so a run of three or more colons still leaves `::` in the logged reason.
  WHY: This breaks the `"::" not in match.group(1)` invariant of test_graphql_failure_reason_is_logged for malformed stderr (latent, because the fixture does not exercise it), and the security risk is small; rated NIT (mapped to low); anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite raised the same point only as hardening suggestions.
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:806-820 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When `gh_retry gh api graphql` succeeds but the `jq -e` validation at line 816 fails, promote_cycle_hold_history returns 1 at line 820 without removing `err_file`.
  WHY: Each malformed-but-not-error GraphQL response leaks one mktemp file, at most one per cycle (bounded, not security-sensitive); rated NIT (mapped to low).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
(No task gaps reported.)
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:pin_preflight(), lines 567-572; unpinned path at lines 1072-1076 and 1101-1128 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The check `if [ -n "${PROMOTE_CYCLE_HOLD_RELEASED_ISSUES}" ]; then PIN_PREFLIGHT_REASON=released_cycle_holds_pin; return 1; fi` makes a releasing tick always run unpinned. It sits before the wrapper and support checks, and it applies even while the parked cycle's `promote-cycle-frozen` tag still exists; scripts/promote_candidate_follow.sh (lines 203-227) keeps `promote-candidate` frozen and deletes the tag only after `PROMOTE_CYCLE_FREEZE_MAX_SECS` (default 172800), and never deletes a lightweight or unparsable tag (line 213).
  WHY: A release 24-48h after the freeze dispatches the gate on `main` with baseline `main_tip`, while the `@promote-candidate` wrappers run the old frozen code, so the cycle promotes a `main` SHA that neither orchestrator run exercised; `test_released_tick_runs_the_cycle_unpinned` never sets `pin_tag_exists`. Suggested fix: read `git/ref/tags/${PROMOTE_CYCLE_PIN_TAG}` and, if the tag exists, keep holding with `skip_cycle cycle_in_flight "tracking_issues=<released> detail=freeze_tag_held"`; run unpinned only on a 404; add a test with `pin_tag_exists: True`.
- Task completeness: NONE. All files_touched are present and P4 "A latched tracking issue older than the cap no longer holds the cycle and is reported" is implemented; the reviewer rejected the pass-1 TASK_GAP from z-ai_glm-5_3-flash as coming from a broken prompt.
- Performance: NONE. The reviewer treats the summed 30s alert waits as speculative.
- HARDENING: scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh promote_cycle_hold_guard, release arm: each released issue makes a blocking alert call of up to 30s; send one combined alert after the loop, or stop alerting after the first timeout (est. 5 lines).
- HARDENING: scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh promote_cycle_hold_history, err_line `sed 's/::/: :/g'`: `:::` still leaves `::`; use `tr -s ':'` before the sed, or `sed 's/:/: /g'` (est. 1 line).
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:pin_preflight() (lines 564-575) and promote_cycle_hold_guard() (lines 910-936) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The cycle is forced unpinned (`PIN_PREFLIGHT_REASON=released_cycle_holds_pin`) whenever a tracking issue is released, even if a `promote-cycle-frozen` tag exists and pinning is otherwise enabled.
  WHY: The smoke gate runs on the `main` tip while the proving and verifying runs use the frozen `promote-candidate` branch through the pinned wrappers, which bypasses the pinned-mode verification guarantee.
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:promote_cycle_hold_guard() (lines 910-936) calls promote_cycle_hold_alert() in a loop | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `promote_cycle_hold_alert()` waits synchronously for up to 30 seconds for each Telegram alert.
  WHY: With many released issues (e.g. 20+), the total delay (potentially more than 10 minutes) can exceed the remaining runtime margin, and the workflow is killed on timeout.
- HARDENING: scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh promote_cycle_hold_history() (line 793): the `sed 's/::/: :/g'` and `cut` pipeline may not reliably handle every `::` case; use `tr`, or sanitise the prefix in one pass (est. 1 line).
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:lines 569-572 (`pin_preflight` new branch), 936 (synchronous call site), 1072-1076/1101-1128 (unpinned dispatch path); interacts with .github/workflows/internal-orchestrate.yml:37 and scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:582 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `released_cycle_holds_pin` branch returns early at line 571, before the wrapper-pin check at line 582; the gate dispatches on `main` (line 1125) with `cycle_baseline_sha=${main_tip}` (line 1102), but the proving run goes through `APPLY_ANALYSIS_DISPATCHER` (line 1200), then scripts/apply_analysis_on_main.sh:121, then internal-orchestrate.yml:37, which is pinned to `orchestrate.yml@promote-candidate`.
  WHY: While the tag exists, `@promote-candidate` stays frozen on the old commit (48h freeze cap against a 24h hold cap), so the gate tests new `main` code while the orchestrator runs old code; the branch assumes that with pin mode off the wrappers follow `main`, which they do not (header comment at scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:64).
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:lines 754-775 (`promote_cycle_hold_alert`), 936 (call site) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Each synchronous alert call in the release loop polls every 0.2s up to `limit=150` (line 764) and blocks for up to 30s; the curl in scripts/tg_helpers.sh:131 has no `--max-time`.
  WHY: With N>=21 released issues (the `per_page=100` listing is at line 972), N*30 seconds is 10.5 minutes or more, which exceeds the 10-minute margin under `timeout-minutes: 340` (.github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml:126, comment at lines 124-125); the 30s bound prevents indefinite hangs but not cumulative ones.
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:line 810, sanitization pipeline `sed 's/::/: :/g'` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The non-overlapping `g` replacement turns `::::::` into output that still contains `::`.
  WHY: The `assert "::" not in match.group(1)` check in test_graphql_failure_reason_is_logged fails on multi-colon stderr; the fixture `"HTTP 404: Not Found\n"` does not exercise this, so the gap is latent; the security risk is small.
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:line 806 (`err_file="$(mktemp)"`), 815, 811; missing cleanup when `jq -e` at line 816 fails before the return at line 820 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `err_file` is not removed when the GraphQL call succeeds but the `jq -e` validation fails.
  WHY: One temp file leaks per malformed response, at most once per cycle.
- HARDENING: line 936: dispatch the alerts in the background and wait on the collected PIDs with a single 30s timeout (~8 lines, HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3).
- HARDENING: line 810: repeat the sed until no `::` remains, or use `tr -s ':' | sed 's/:/: /g'` (1 line, HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1).
- HARDENING: lines 806-820: use a single cleanup point or a trap for `err_file` (3 lines, HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1).
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
